decisive_items: complex cystic mass in the pancreatic head
calcifications, enhancing septa, millimetric nodules, and soft-tissue components
cystic lesion in the uncinate process
response.rationale: IPMN commonly arises in the pancreatic head/uncinate and can present as a complex cystic mass with calcifications, septa, and mural nodules. MCN is less likely due to typical body/tail location and female predominance; SPN usually affects younger women; serous cystadenoma typically shows microcysts and central scar; pancreatic cancer is usually solid.

rejected.why: Serous cystadenoma typically has microcystic architecture and central scar, not mural nodules or soft-tissue components.
Pancreatic cancer is usually solid; cystic presentation with calcifications and septa is atypical.
MCN is classically located in the pancreatic body/tail, not the head/uncinate, and often lacks calcifications.
SPN predominantly affects young women and typically has a solid-cystic appearance with hemorrhage, less fitting this age and imaging.
